name: Trinidad and Tobago
summary_text: Trinidad and Tobago demands real caution from trans visitors — legally improved, socially dangerous. The courts struck down the colonial buggery laws (Jones v. AG, 2018, upheld on appeal), removing criminalisation of same-sex intimacy; but there is no legal gender recognition, no SOGI anti-discrimination protection, and parliament has repeatedly rejected reforms (the ruling party's constitution review again refused SOGI protections in 2024). Documented street risk is substantial: community advocates report trans people are still “beaten, stoned and chopped,” with most incidents never reported; and police have publicly warned of a spate of Grindr ambush robberies — criminals using fake profiles to lure LGBT victims to meetings followed by armed robbery (multiple cases through 2023-2024, including a Cocorite man beaten and robbed). This dating-app predation pattern is a direct traveler concern.

sources.claim_summary: Trinidad and Tobago Newsday (July 2024): 'Long way yet for recognition, safe spaces' - TT Transgender Coalition director Rae Alibey says the trans community is the most marginalised and not even recognised in T&T; gender identity is not recognised separately from sexual orientation; gender-identity markers on institutional forms are absent; national discussions and attitudinal research needed.

Newsday (Nov 2024): police warning over cyber criminals - Grindr hook-ups ending in cars, cash and phones stolen; criminals create fake dating accounts to lure LGBT+ victims into meetings followed by armed robbery, beatings or sexual assault; two separate incidents reported in one week.

Newsday editorial (June 2024): 'Grind hate to a halt' - a spate of Grindr-related attacks (almost half a dozen in recent months); Supt Claire Guy-Alleyne points to gaps in the law: 'We don't have a specific hate crime category in legislation'; the editorial argues the gap must be closed.

sources.title: CAISO head unhappy LGBTQ rights reform ignored again - CNC3
sources.claim_summary: CNC3 (Aug 2024): CAISO head unhappy LGBTQ rights reform ignored again - the PNM Constitution Review Committee rejected reform of sexual-orientation rights; CAISO had recommended adding sexual orientation and gender identity to protected statuses under section 4 of the Constitution; 'no political party has stepped up'.

sources.title: Gay Life in Trinidad & Tobago - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Life in Trinidad & Tobago' (Aug 2012): although homosexuality is illegal, 'the laws are mostly ignored' - context of the islands' history from Spanish colonisation through British rule.

sources.title: This man needs your help to take on his country's government and decriminalise homosexuality | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Nov 2017) by Jason Jones: 'I am a criminal simply because I am a gay man' - his High Court challenge to Trinidad and Tobago's laws (up to 25 years for 'serious indecency'); ~100,000 LGBT people live under the threat; the laws were inherited from Britain but extended to lesbians after independence.

sources.title: Despite his claims, Trinidad leader clings to anti-LGBT laws
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (June 2016): PM Keith Rowley claimed the state must protect all citizens 'regardless of whom they sleep with', but said there were no plans to amend the buggery laws and declined to address the EOC's call for anti-discrimination protection.
